repositories.name: quinoa
repositories.description: Adaptive computational fluid dynamics

paragraphs: Quinoa is a set of computational tools that enables research and numerical analysis in fluid dynamics. Using the Charm++ runtime system, we employ asynchronous (or non-blocking) parallel programming and decompose computational problems into a large number of work units (that may be more than the available number of processors) enabling arbitrary overlap of parallel computation, communication, input, and output. Then the runtime system dynamically and automatically homogenizes computational load across the simulation distributed across many computers.

Our ultimate goal is to simulate large and complex engineering multiphysics problems with a production-quality code that is extensible and maintainable, using hardware resources efficiently, even for problems with a priori unknown, heterogeneous, and dynamic load distribution.
This software has been acknowledged by the U.S. Department of Energy / National Nuclear Security Administration for open source release, O4963.

paragraphs: Securely store your passwords in your Google Drive.

Password Keeper is a web app that can be used to store your passwords or other account details in your Google Drive. The data is store in an encrypted format and can only be decrypted using a master password that you set during first login.

For storing all the encrypted passwords a Google Sheet stored in your Google Drive is used as a database. Since, Google provides REST API to manipulate Google Sheet the web-app could directly interact with data stored in Google Sheet.

repositories.name: crdt-text-simulator
repositories.description: Two collaborative text replicas on an RGA CRDT: diverge, sync, converge, live in the browser

paragraphs: Two text editors on one page, both free to type at once. Let them diverge, then press Sync now and watch every operation travel between the replicas until both show exactly the same text. Under the hood it is a Replicated Growable Array (RGA), the same family of algorithm that powers collaborative editors like Figma's multiplayer mode and Google Docs style merging.

"Real-time collaboration" looks like magic until you meet the two impossible questions underneath it: what happens when two people type at the same spot at the same time, and what happens when one person deletes a letter that another person is typing next to? Conflict-free Replicated Data Types answer both with clever ordering instead of locking, and this playground lets you cause the conflicts yourself and watch the resolution happen. It is also a genuinely correct CRDT: the fuzz tests hammer it with hundreds of concurrent random edits and assert that every replica converges to identical…
The banner always tells you the truth about the state: how many operations each replica holds that the other has never seen, and whether the texts currently agree.

paragraphs: A free online simulator with a virtual FPGA board. Flip the switches while your design runs, and watch the LEDs respond.
Try it online · Download for Windows · Host it yourself

HDLBoard is a free, open-source online VHDL and Verilog simulator for learning digital logic and FPGA design. It combines real HDL simulation with an interactive virtual Terasic DE1-SoC FPGA board. After the first visit, a service worker caches the app so it also works offline.

paragraphs: 🚀 KQ-LMPC is the fastest open-source Koopman MPC controller for quadrotors: zero training data, fully explainable, hardware-proven SE(3) control.
⚡ Real-time convex MPC (<10 ms) • ✅ Stability guarantees • 🔧 PX4/ROS2 ready
Real-time control of agile aerial robots is still dominated by slow NMPC or black-box learning-based controllers. One is too computationally heavy, the other is unsafe without guarantees.
features: ✅ Analytical Koopman lifting with generalizable observables → No neural networks, no training, no data fitting required
✅ Data-free Koopman-lifted LTI + LPV models → Derived directly from SE(3) quadrotor dynamics using Lie algebra structure
✅ Real-time Linear MPC (LMPC) → Solved as a single convex QP termed KQ-LMPC → < 10 ms solve time on Jetson NX / embedded hardware
✅ Trajectory tracking on SE(3) → Provable controllability in lifted Koopman space
✅ Closed-loop robustness guarantees → Input-to-state practical stability (I-ISpS)

Bezug zu OR: ein Depot-Effekt, der nicht an einzelnen Lieferungen hängen bleibt (keine Leckage), ist eine ehrlichere Grundlage für die Standortplanung – eine Kodierung, die nur auf wenigen Lieferungen je Depot beruht, würde sonst zufällige Schwankungen für ein echtes Standortmerkmal halten.

Einordnung in die Reihe: jedes vorige Stück hat die Split-Suche oder Regularisierung verändert (Varianz → regularisierter Gain → Histogramme/blattweise) - CatBoost stellt eine andere Frage: woher kommt der Gradient, den ein Baum lernt? Dieselbe Falle gibt es bei kategorischen Merkmalen (naives Target Encoding). CatBoosts Antwort: nie mit dem eigenen Etikett einer Zeile rechnen - geordnetes Boosting und geordnete Target Statistics. Dazu: vollständig…

paragraphs: Siebtes Stück der Spannbaum-Reihe der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning". Ein Depot (Konzentrator, Werk) versorgt Kunden über ein Leitungsnetz, aber jeder Zweig unter einer Depotkante darf nur Q Bedarfseinheiten tragen - eine Leitung, ein Port, ein Verteilerkabel hat begrenzte Kapazität. Ohne Grenze ist der Baum der MST, bei Q = 1 der Stern; dazwischen ist das Problem NP-schwer (Papadimitriou 1978, schon bei Einheitsbedarf). Die Standard-Heuristik ist Esau-Williams (1966): Start mit dem Stern, dann immer die Verschmelzung zweier…

repositories.name: guided-local-search-demo
repositories.description: Guided Local Search an derselben Lieferroute – Sehen Sie das Gegenstück zu Tabu Search: statt Kanten für eine feste Zahl Iterationen zu verbieten, bekommt jede Tourkante eine Strafzahl, die nie verfällt. Interaktive Streamlit-Demo, Teil von sebastianhanisch.net

paragraphs: Zwölftes Stück der Trajektorien-Metaheuristiken-Linie der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning": dieselbe Rundtour wie in der hill-climbing-demo und der tabu-search-demo (ein Depot, n Kundenstopps in einem 100 × 100-km-Gebiet), dieselbe untere Schranke, dieselbe volle-2-opt-Nachbarschaft und dieselbe Bewertungs-Zählweise wie Tabu Search.

Einordnung in die Reihe: Guided Local Search (Voudouris & Tsang 1999) ist ein direktes Kind von Hill Climbing, wie Simulated Annealing, ILS/VNS, Tabu Search und GRASP - und der direkte Kontrast zu Tabu Search: dasselbe Problem (über ein lokales Optimum hinauskommen, ohne Struktur wegzuwerfen), der entgegengesetzte Mechanismus. Tabu Search verbietet die zuletzt entfernten Kanten für eine feste Zahl Iterationen (Gedächtnis, das verfällt). Guided Local Search bestraft stattdessen Tourkanten in der Zielfunktion selbst (Länge + λ · Strafen) - eine Strafe, die nie verfällt. Googles…

Ergebnis in Kürze: Unter 100 Tausend Vorschlägen ist Guided Local Search mit Tabu Search nahezu IDENTISCH - ab 200 Tausend zieht es klar davon, und der Abstand zur Schranke schrumpft mit jeder Budget-Verdopplung stärker als bei Tabu Search (der absolute Vorsprung bleibt ab 500 Tausend bei etwa 1.4-1.5 Prozentpunkten). 60 Stopps, Lambda 5 (kalibriert): bei 10-50 Tausend Vorschlägen liegen beide Verfahren auf zwei Nachkommastellen genau gleichauf (287.75 % gegen Tabus 287.8 % bei 10 Tausend) - beide sind volle-Nachbarschaft-Verfahren, und bei so wenigen Iterationen hat die dauerhafte Strafe…

repositories.name: moore-hodgson-demo
repositories.description: Moore-Hodgson: möglichst wenige Aufträge verspäten – Ergebnis in Kürze: Moore-Hodgson trifft auf jeder getesteten Instanz exakt das Minimum der Vollaufzählung. Interaktive Streamlit-Demo, Teil von sebastianhanisch.net

paragraphs: Drittes Stück der Klassische-Scheduling-Theorie-Linie der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning": $n$ Aufträge mit Bearbeitungszeit $pj$ und Fälligkeit $dj$ auf einer Maschine, Ziel ist die ANZAHL verspäteter Aufträge zu minimieren ($1||\sum Uj$) – anders als $L{\max}$ im vorigen Stück zählt hier jeder verspätete Auftrag gleich viel, egal wie spät.

Einordnung in die Linie: Moore-Hodgson (Moore 1968) ist der erste "zweistufige" Algorithmus dieser Linie – nicht nur sortieren wie SPT/EDD, sondern sortieren UND gezielt streichen. Aufträge nach EDD einplanen; sobald einer verspätet würde, wird NICHT dieser Auftrag entfernt, sondern der mit der GRÖSSTEN Bearbeitungszeit unter allen bisher eingeplanten – ein zweiter, unabhängig interessanter Mechanismus, der genau erklärt, warum "streiche den Auslöser" die falsche Intuition wäre.

Ergebnis in Kürze: Moore-Hodgson trifft auf jeder getesteten Instanz (n = 2 bis 9) exakt das Minimum der Vollaufzählung. Bei 20 Aufträgen hält Moore-Hodgson im Mittel 5,2 Aufträge mehr pünktlich als EDD (die für dieses Ziel falsche Regel) und 6,5 mehr als eine zufällige Reihenfolge. Der ehrliche Bruch: auf dem Werkstatt/Logistik-Vehikel (Rüstzeiten zwischen Familien) bleibt Moore-Hodgson bei Rüstzeit 0 exakt optimal (Konsistenz-Test), aber der Abstand zum echten Minimum wächst mit der Rüstzeit – bis zu 2,2 zusätzlich verspätete Aufträge im Mittel bei 60 Minuten je Familienwechsel.

whatItDoes.text: Drittes Stück der Klassische-Scheduling-Theorie-Linie der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning": $n$ Aufträge mit Bearbeitungszeit $pj$ und Fälligkeit $dj$ auf einer Maschine, Ziel ist die ANZAHL verspäteter Aufträge zu minimieren ($1||\sum Uj$) – anders als $L{\max}$ im vorigen Stück zählt hier jeder verspätete Auftrag gleich viel, egal wie spät.

Die Stücke 3 bis 5 (mmc-queue-demo, erlang-a-demo, square-root-staffing-demo) nahmen eine konstante Ankunftsrate an. Hier schwankt sie in einer Welle. Advisory only. It doesn't process transactions or government applications.

A lot of the AI-for-agriculture projects I'd seen were English-only and assumed the user was comfortable with an app or a dashboard. That's not who actually needs this — most of the people who'd benefit from quick disease diagnosis or same-day mandi prices are dealing with all of it in a regional language, often over a basic phone. So the two things I prioritized were RAG-grounded answers (so it's not guessing about pesticide dosages) and multilingual support, over adding more features. The guardrail layer came out of the same instinct — a farming bot confidently answering something outside…

paragraphs: Autonomous code generation, execution, debugging, and testing — powered by LangGraph + Groq

AutoDevAgent is a multi-agent AI system that takes a natural language task description and autonomously writes, runs, debugs, and tests Python or SQL code — without any manual intervention. It uses a LangGraph state machine to coordinate nine specialised agents, each responsible for one step of the software development loop: planning, generation, execution, error classification, debugging, test generation, explanation, and flowchart diagramming. The system is designed for developers who want to see how agentic AI handles real code quality requirements — not just code generation, but…
features: Clarification gate — before running anything, checks if the task is specific enough. If ambiguous, asks one targeted question and waits for the user's answer before proceeding.
Non-coding gate — rejects general knowledge questions with a friendly message. Only blocks on high/medium confidence to avoid false positives.
Scope gate — rejects full-project requests ("build a YouTube app"). Any single SQL query is always in-scope regardless of complexity.
Language auto-detection — fast 8B model classifies Python vs SQL. User can override via radio button at any time.

Task-aware model routing — analyses the task and assigns the best model to each agent role. Reasoning-heavy and SQL tasks route Llama 3.3 70B to the generator and debugger; planning, tests, and explanation always use…

repositories.name: style-dictionary
repositories.description: A build system for creating cross-platform styles.

paragraphs: A Style Dictionary uses design tokens to define styles once and use those styles on any platform or language. It provides a single place to create and edit your styles, and exports these tokens to all the places you need - iOS, Android, CSS, JS, HTML, sketch files, style documentation, etc. It is available as a CLI through npm, but can also be used like any normal node module if you want to extend its functionality.

When you are managing user experiences, it can be quite challenging to keep styles consistent and synchronized across multiple development platforms and devices. At the same time, designers, developers, PMs and others must be able to have consistent and up-to-date style documentation to enable effective work and communication. Even then, mistakes inevitably happen and the design may not be implemented accurately. Style Dictionary solves this by automatically generating style definitions across all platforms from a single source - removing roadblocks, errors, and inefficiencies across your…

A stepper motor pushes the filter disc through a spring-loaded friction clutch, an AS5600 magnetic sensor reads where the disc actually is, and an ESP32-S3 talks to your imaging software. Nothing is cut away from the original wheel: the motorisation clamps around it, and it can come off again.

It was designed around a manual five-position wheel for 2-inch filters, a StarDikor — that is the wheel in every picture, and the wheel every measurement was taken from. It is not tied to it: the CAD is parametric, and Not all wheels are the same below says which handful of numbers describe yours.
features: An ASCOM / Alpaca driver — only if there is demand for it. Wheelly speaks

whatItDoes.text: A motorised filter wheel for astrophotography, made out of a manual one.

repositories.name: vibey
repositories.description: Open-source orchestrator for AI coding agents: a spec interview, unattended builds on local (Ollama) or paid agents, human-gated review, and an append-only PostgreSQL ledger so a crashed agent's work is picked up, not lost.

paragraphs: AI coding agents can write the code. Getting it delivered still takes a person: re-prompting an agent that lost the thread, re-explaining everything after a crash, restarting the run when one vendor's credits give out at 2 a.m.

vibey is a free, open-source orchestrator for AI coding agents — a program that runs a team of them for you. It interviews you until the specification is precise, builds unattended on local or paid agents, stops only for the decisions that are yours, and writes every step to a record that can only be added to — an append-only ledger in a PostgreSQL database — so a crashed or out-of-credit agent's work is picked up again rather than lost.

Never written code? You can still read this. Code is text files of instructions computers run; an AI coding agent is a program that writes and edits that code from plain-English requests; deploying means putting the finished software somewhere people can use it. vibey's job is to manage a team of those agents from your first description to deployed software, the way a project manager runs a team — asking you questions up front, checking the work, and only interrupting you when a decision is truly yours.
features: A crash loses no job. Jobs are held under expiring leases and reclaimed when a worker dies. A chaos test runs 8 workers through 500 jobs, abandoning each claim with probability 0.2, and passes only if no job is lost or…

The record cannot be quietly rewritten. The database refuses every update and delete to the ledger (ADR-0055), and a SHA-256 hash chain over its events makes any edit visible (ledgerchain.py). See one for yourself in…
Local first, paid by choice. The default engine runs GPT-OSS 20B on your own machine through Ollama (ADR-0064); a paid engine runs only when no local one can (ADR-0038).
You decide what matters. Design, review and deployment wait for your recorded answer, and a waiting question parks its job instead of blocking a worker (ADR-0009).

Held to gates it cannot talk its way past. vibey's four code layers each need 100% branch coverage to merge (ADR-0023), every hard call is argued in a decision record (90 ADRs), and releases publish through PyPI trusted…

requirements.text: It interviews you until the specification is precise, builds unattended on local or paid agents, stops only for the decisions that are yours, and writes every step to a record that can only be added to — an append-only ledger in a PostgreSQL database — so a crashed or out-of-credit agent's work is picked up again rather than lost.
The default engine runs GPT-OSS 20B on your own machine through Ollama (ADR-0064); a paid engine runs only when no local one can (ADR-0038).

paragraphs: An agentic AI system that autonomously routes queries between document retrieval, vector search, and live web search to generate grounded, cited answers.

FAISS retrieval: the only backend the live agent queries, with L2-normalized embeddings for cosine similarity. retrieval/pineconestore.py and retrieval/llamaindexloader.py are standalone reference implementations of…

Session memory with LangGraph checkpointing across all turns in a session, MemorySaver by default (process-local, not persisted across restarts), or agent/memory.py's AsyncPostgresSaver when CHECKPOINTDSN is set, so…

Optional Redis response cache (agent/cache.py) - when REDISURL is set, an identical query on a fresh session (no prior conversation context to honour) is served from Redis instead of re-running the graph, with a TTL…
Real-time streaming responses via FastAPI Server-Sent Events (SSE) with token-level output

requirements.text: No API keys and no .env are required, every test runs offline.

paragraphs: A quantitative, governed fitness function for microservice boundary granularity.

Fulcrum fuses three signals normally analyzed in isolation into one bounded, diagnostic, per-boundary score, the RVx Index, that tells you whether a service boundary adds value or is a distributed monolith:
features: Kinetic Efficiency (E) - runtime overhead from distributed traces (useful time / total time).
Semantic Distinctness (S) - evolutionary independence from version-control co-change.
Cognitive Load (L) - maintenance complexity normalized against team capacity (Conway's Law made measurable).

whatItDoes.text: A quantitative, governed fitness function for microservice boundary granularity.

paragraphs: RECOVER-AI is an autonomous, policy-bounded AI subscription revenue recovery engine designed to address involuntary churn caused by failed recurring payments.

Instead of relying entirely on rigid recovery rules, RECOVER-AI uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to diagnose payment failure context and propose recovery actions such as payment retries, payment links, and Promise-to-Pay (P2P) workflows.
The system does not allow the LLM to directly execute financial actions. AI-generated decisions are passed through a deterministic Policy Gatekeeper and a Finite State Machine (FSM) before execution.

repositories.description: Free, open-source web app: binaural beats that adapt to your breathing in real time for sleep, focus & meditation. Runs in your browser, no signup.

paragraphs: Free, open-source, no signup, no install. Vuko generates binaural beats with the Web Audio API and — if you allow microphone access — listens to your breathing rhythm and adapts the beat frequency to it in real time. Everything runs locally in your browser; no audio ever leaves your device.

Every binaural beats app plays a fixed frequency at you. Vuko closes the loop: it detects your breathing through the microphone and nudges the beat frequency along with you — slowing as you slow down. Pick a target state and Vuko guides you there:

Plus a built-in library of ambient tracks with semantic search — type what you feel like ("rain on a tent", "temple bells") and it finds matching music via sentence-transformer embeddings, entirely client-side.

repositories.name: FerroUI
repositories.description: Cross-platform UI framework for Rust: styled property system, data binding, XAML, control themes and a composition renderer. A port of Avalonia.

paragraphs: FerroUI is a cross-platform UI framework for Rust: a retained-mode control library with a styled property system, data binding, XAML markup, control themes and a composition-based renderer. It is a port of the Avalonia UI framework to Rust that keeps the original architecture, contracts and behaviour, so that applications, themes and markup written against that model carry over with their structure intact.

Status: 0.3.0, with the preview 0.4.0-preview.1. 0.3.0, which adds ports of Rx, DynamicData and ReactiveUI for MVVM applications (docs/mvvm.md), is the current release on crates.io. 0.4.0-preview.1 previews the next one: it adds a declarative Rust API for user interfaces without XAML, with builders, the rsx! macro and signals (docs/declarative-ui.md), and makes the Vello backend faster (CHANGELOG.md). Every upstream file and member in scope is ported or waived with a recorded reason. The framework runs on macOS, Windows, Linux (X11, Wayland and the framebuffer), iOS, Android and in the…

The ControlCatalog sample with the WinUI 3 theme (ferroui-themes-winui), its default theme, on Windows 11 with the Mica backdrop. Text is shaped with HarfBuzz and drawn by Skia with the platform's text rendering settings: the contrast and gamma of ClearType on Windows, greyscale antialiasing on a high-density display, and colour emoji (docs/porting/text-rendering.md).
features: Complete object model. Styled and direct properties with value priorities, inheritance, coercion and change notification; logical and visual trees; routed events; layout; input, focus and gestures.
Styling and theming. Selectors, styles, control themes, resources, theme variants and transitions. The Fluent, Simple and WinUI 3 themes are included.
Data binding. Compiled and reflection-style binding paths, converters, multi-bindings, data validation and templates.
XAML. A port of the XamlX compiler front end with the framework's transformers and markup extensions. Documents are compiled to Rust source by the build script of a crate, or loaded at run time.
Composition renderer. A compositor with a render loop on its own thread, dirty-region tracking, server-side visuals and composition animations, drawing through a backend-neutral drawing context.

whatItDoes.text: FerroUI is a cross-platform UI framework for Rust: a retained-mode control library with a styled property system, data binding, XAML markup, control themes and a composition-based renderer. It is a port of the Avalonia UI framework to Rust that keeps the original architecture, contracts and behaviour, so that applications, themes and markup written against that model carry over with their structure intact.

repositories.name: table-file-format
repositories.description: An open data matrix file format

paragraphs: .table is an open file format for the tables people build in Airtable, Notion or a spreadsheet: typed columns, linked tables, formulas, and views such as boards and calendars.

What's different is where it lives. A .table is a file on your own disk, not a workspace on someone else's server. Inside it is plain text: a schema, and one line per row. Any tool can read it, git can track it, and you never need the app that made it to get your data back.
It is for people who work with information, not only for developers. Opened in an app, it looks and edits like the tools you already know.

repositories.description: Blazing fast fuzzy text search for Python.

paragraphs: Blazing fast, lightweight and customizable fuzzy and semantic text search in Python.
Neofuzz is a fuzzy search library based on vectorization and approximate nearest neighbour search techniques.

Most fuzzy search libraries rely on optimizing the hell out of the same couple of fuzzy search algorithms (Hamming distance, Levenshtein distance). Sometimes unfortunately due to the complexity of these algorithms, no amount of optimization will get you the speed, that you want.

repositories.name: drafty
repositories.description: Kanban board with a blueprint, pointer-based drag & drop and Motion animations. Vanilla JS, no build, offline PWA.

paragraphs: Drafty is a Kanban board styled like a technical drawing. It is written in plain JavaScript with no framework and no build step, and the interface is in Spanish.

The interesting part is the interaction layer: drag and drop is built on pointer events instead of the HTML5 drag API, the board re-renders by reconciling keyed nodes, and every change goes through one function that records history, saves and redraws. All of it works with the keyboard and offline.
features: Three columns (to do, in progress, done) and several boards in tabs. Boards can be created, renamed with a double click and deleted.
Cards with a title, priority, label and due date. Overdue cards are flagged.
Drag and drop with mouse or touch (long press on touch). Esc cancels a drag, and the page scrolls when you drag near the top or bottom edge.
Undo and redo with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, up to 100 steps. Deleting a card also shows an "Undo" toast.
Live search by title, label or card code (for example TK-007).

whatItDoes.text: Drafty is a Kanban board styled like a technical drawing. It is written in plain JavaScript with no framework and no build step, and the interface is in Spanish.

requirements.text: There are no accounts, analytics or third-party requests.
